title: Inference Advisor — UX lifecycle & wireframe notes
summary: Working draft for an in-console 'Inference Advisor' that surfaces batching, caching, and quantization suggestions tailored to a model + route. Includes wireframe annotations, interaction flows, and an initial groomed backlog with acceptance criteria and telemetry hooks.
content:
Context and goal:
- Problem: teams run into opaque cost/latency tradeoffs when picking batching, caching, or quantization settings. We want a single advisor panel that gives actionable suggestions for saving token-cost and improving p99 latency without sacrificing quality.
- Audience: platform engineers and product ML owners who use Redwood Console to tune serving.
- Proposed product surface: an 'Inference Advisor' card inside the Route detail page (and standalone Workbench) that contains:
  - Quick summary (est. monthly $ delta, est p99 change, likely quality impact)
  - Ranked suggestions: batching, prefix/KV cache, model quantization profile, and TTLs for cache entries
  - Preview / diff for a single request: show how tokens/latency change with suggestion applied
  - Quick apply + preview + rollback for Dedicated/Private customers
  - Link-outs to detailed docs and eval sets used for quality impact checks

Wireframe notes (sketch-level):
- Header area: small badge showing 'advisor confidence' (low / medium / high) driven by sample size and traffic variance. Add tooltip explaining confidence.
- Left column (context): route name, model version pinned, sample traffic distribution (seq len CDF), tokens per request median, p50/p95/p99 latency.
- Middle column (suggestions list): collapsible suggestion cards. Each card shows: title (e.g., "Increase batch size to 64"), category (batching/caching/quant), estimated savings, estimated impact on p99, quality risk (low/medium/high), confidence score, data window used.
  - Each card has three CTA buttons: "Preview", "Apply to canary", "Add to backlog".
- Right column (preview pane): when a suggestion is selected, show a diffs panel with per-request token counts, estimated server CPU/GPU usage delta, and sample outputs for 3 prompts (baseline vs suggested). Include small quality check indicators (e.g., embedding similarity delta or perplexity proxy).
- Inline microcopy: call out assumptions ("estimates based on last 7 days of route traffic — highly variable traffic may reduce accuracy").

Interaction flow (happy path):
1) User opens Route -> Advisor. Advisor shows 3 ranked suggestions.
2) User clicks "Preview" on batching suggestion. Right pane renders token/latency delta and two sample outputs.
3) User clicks "Apply to canary". A modal appears to configure canary size (default 10% traffic) and duration. Show SLO guardrails (abort if p99 > baseline * 1.2 or error rate +0.5%).
4) Canary runs; metrics stream into Console. Advisor updates with actual observed delta and auto-tags suggestion status (succeeded/failed).
5) User clicks "Promote" to full route or "Rollback".

Edge cases and constraints:
- Private customers: Advisor can only suggest quantization profiles that match available hardware (we must consult the infra catalog).
- Cold routes / low traffic: show 'insufficient data' and offer a small synthetic eval run using customer prompt set if available.
- Safety: never auto-apply quantization on routes that have flagged eval regressions above threshold. 
- Model types: LLaMA-like vs transformer-mixture models might need separate kernel-level flags — surface 'compatibility warnings' when necessary.

Telemetry and data used (initial set):
- Inputs: last N days of tokens, sequence length histogram, per-token latency distribution, failure/error counts, model version, region.
- Outputs (to display): est token savings (tokens/day and $/month), est p99 change (ms), confidence (sample size / variance), quality delta approximation (embedding sim or discrete eval set results).
- Events to track: suggestion_shown, suggestion_previewed, suggestion_applied_canary, canary_promoted, canary_rolled_back, suggestion_added_to_backlog.

Groomed backlog (short list, prioritized):
- OPT-201: Advisor baseline telemetry plumbing (7d) — EPIC (owner: Marco). AC: panel shows p50/p95/p99 + seq len CDF.
- OPT-202: Batching suggestion engine (heuristics v1) — estimate 3pt. AC: produce suggestion card with est savings and confidence computed from traffic percentiles.
- OPT-203: On-demand synthetic eval runner for low-traffic routes — AC: allow upload of up to 100 prompts; run locally against quantized variant and show sim scores.
- OPT-204: Canary orchestration UI + abort rules — AC: modal to configure canary and abort if SLOs exceeded. Integrate with rollout system (product-console team).
- OPT-205: Quantization compatibility matrix + kernel warnings — AC: show compatibility badge per suggestion and block apply on incompatible infra.
- OPT-206: Suggestion inbox / backlog page — AC: allow product managers to triage suggestions created across routes.

Acceptance criteria (example for OPT-202 Batching v1):
- System surfaces a "Increase batch size" suggestion when median seq len < 512 and current batch < suggested batch and throughput above 10rps.
- Estimated token savings within ±30% of observed after a 24-hour canary for 60% of routes in pilot.
- UI displays confidence and data window used.

Open questions / decisions needed (notes to self):
- Quality proxy: use embedding cosine similarity vs running customer evals — tradeoffs: cost vs signal. Which default? (ask Research team).
- Pricing calc: use list token_cost or customer-specific negotiated rate? For simplicity start with list price and surface caveat.
- Canary defaults: 10% x 24h? 15% x 12h? Ops and SRE input needed.
- Rollout automation: should 'Promote' be a single click or require approval for enterprise customers?

Mock copy and microcopy drafts (short bits to include in wireframes):
- Advisor header: "Inference Advisor — suggestions to reduce cost or improve latency based on recent traffic patterns"
- Confidence tooltip: "Confidence is calculated from the sample size and variability in the last 7 days. Low confidence indicates estimates may be noisy."
- Preview CTA tooltip: "See estimated token/latency impact and sample outputs before applying change."

Accessibility and localization notes:
- All badges must have aria-labels explaining the meaning (e.g., "confidence: high").
- Microcopy should be translatable; avoid idioms.

Next steps / immediate TODOs (this sprint):
- [ ] Sync with Research to pick quality proxy (owner: Grace) by 2025-02-20.
- [ ] Backend: instrument per-route seq len histogram and token cost calc (owner: Marco) by 2025-02-28.
- [ ] Design: produce high-fidelity mockups for the advisor card and preview pane (owner: Priya) by 2025-03-03.
- [ ] Eng: prototype batching suggestion engine (owner: Omar) — spike to show estimates within 30% on 5 pilot routes by 2025-03-10.

Notes / loose thoughts (brainstorm style):
- Could surface "retro suggestions" where Advisor replays last 30d and shows missed opportunities (e.g., "You could've saved $X/month if batching had been 48"). Useful for PLG growth nudges.
- Consider a lightweight SDK hook so customers can annotate which prompts are quality-sensitive (e.g., legal text) — would reduce risk of bad quantization suggestions.

References:
- Related internal docs: CONFLUENCE-PLT-482 (Estimator design), OPT-analytics-runbook, infra-catalog (private).
- Example Jira: JIRA-OPT-1293 (workbench integration PRD).

End of doc.

Unresolved / TODO: turn the brainstorm into two separate interactions: "Quick wins" (1-click previews) and "Deep tuning" (multi-metric experiments). Need product review to finalize scope for v1.
